title: Newham Council: Establishing the UK Centre for Artificial Intelligence for the public sector
summary: Newham Council and the University of East London propose using existing data to forecast housing demand and homelessness trends. Better temporary-accommodation planning remains an intended benefit.
account: The council and university describe a proposed AI predictive model that would use existing data to forecast housing demand and homelessness trends. This record concerns that intended function for temporary-accommodation planning. The source reports partnership formation and planned development, without demonstrating deployment or improved housing outcomes. Its figure of more than £20 million in council expenditure describes baseline spending, not an AI saving. A separate procurement and allocation application is only under consideration.
purpose: Forecast housing demand and homelessness trends to support temporary-accommodation planning.
system: Proposed AI housing-demand and homelessness forecasting model
deployer: Newham Council and University of East London

ratings.reason: The council is intended to plan temporary accommodation more effectively using forecasts of housing demand and homelessness. The extent of any planning improvement or saving is unassessed.
Residents who need temporary accommodation are intended to benefit from better service planning. No resulting housing or homelessness improvement is established.

ai_role.statement: The source identifies an intended AI model, existing data inputs, and forecasts of housing demand and homelessness trends. It does not evaluate the model or its contribution to service outcomes.

evidence.citation: Local Government Association, AI case-study bank. Council or project account published by LGA. Hosting and editorial curation do not establish independent outcome evaluation.
